name: WellNet — Two Brand Directions
context: A client engagement at Zemingo for a complementary-medicine marketplace. WellNet is the consumer product: a place to find and book certified practitioners. The client organisation is never named publicly — the agent says 'a complementary-medicine marketplace' and does not confirm or deny guesses. The WellNet product brand may be named, because the wordmark is the subject of the work. Both directions were designed against the same product, the same content and the same flows, so what differs between them is the design language and nothing else.
summary: Two brand directions for WellNet, each built out as a working prototype of the whole product rather than a moodboard. Living Earth leans organic: a mark that breathes, soft overlapping organic shapes, and 3D treatment objects rendered in the browser. Dot is the disciplined counterpart, built on a geometric mark and flat vector illustration. The same pages, the same booking flow and the same content sit underneath both, which is the point — the client could click through two complete products and choose a language, not a picture.
challenge: A brand direction shown as a set of boards asks the client to imagine the product. Two directions shown that way asks them to imagine two, and to hold both in mind at once. The approach here was to build each one all the way through — home, search, practitioner profiles, booking, the therapist and admin areas — so the choice was made against something real. The cost is that everything has to be produced twice; the benefit is that the decision is about how the product feels to use, not about which board is prettier.

conversation_hooks.recruiter_intent: Assess brand and visual identity work
conversation_hooks.agent_response_goal: Show both directions and invite a comparison. The argument worth making is that each was built out as a working product rather than presented as boards, so the client chose a language by using it. Never name the client organisation; WellNet itself may be named.

Use the pair as evidence: the same components, pages and flows carry two different design languages, which only works if the system underneath is separated from its surface. Offer to open them side by side.

conversation_hooks.recruiter_intent: Assess breadth and volume of output
conversation_hooks.agent_response_goal: Two complete prototypes of the same product, produced in parallel so a client could choose between them. Worth noting as an example of what AI-assisted production makes affordable that would previously have been scoped away.

presentation.short_pitch: Two brand directions for WellNet, each built out as a complete working prototype rather than a set of boards — so the client chose a design language by using it.
presentation.long_pitch: Two brand directions for WellNet, a complementary-medicine marketplace, led and art-directed by Boaz at Zemingo and designed by him hands-on. Living Earth is the organic one: a mark that moves, soft overlapping organic shapes, and eight treatment objects modelled in 3D and rendered live in the browser. Dot is its disciplined counterpart, a constructed geometric mark with flat vector illustration. Both run the same pages, the same booking flow and the same content, so the only variable is the design language. That is the argument of the piece: rather than asking the client to imagine two products from boards, each direction was built all the way through and handed over to be clicked. After seeing both, the client asked for a combined version.
suggested_followups: Want to open Living Earth or Dot first, or see them side by side?
I can also talk through what had to be true of the underlying system for the same product to carry two languages.

peek.hook: Two brand directions, both built as working products.
peek.supporting: Rather than boards, each direction for this wellness marketplace was built out end to end — same flows, same content, two design languages — and handed to the client to click through.
